title: Financial institutions

match.reason: The bank point covers investment banks, finance companies and pooled funds at Year 12 depth, while the new point is a Year 9 introduction to deposit-taking institutions such as banks, credit unions and building societies, so it is broader and at a different depth.

draft.title: Financial institutions
card: Financial institutions are organisations that look after money for people and businesses. Banks, credit unions and building societies are three common kinds in Australia.
They take deposits and keep the money safe. People can then take it out when they need it.
They make payments for customers, such as card payments, bill payments and transfers to other accounts.
They also lend money to people and businesses, for example for a home, a car or a new shop.
draft.remember: Financial institutions hold money, move money and lend money.

a.q: Sam puts his wages into an account and pays his phone bill from it. Which two services is the institution providing?
opts: Keeping his money safe and making a payment
Lending him money and insuring his phone
Making a payment and setting his wages
Keeping his money safe and borrowing from him
a.why: The account holds Sam's deposit safely, and paying the bill is a payment made for him. Lending is a different service, because Sam is not borrowing anything here.
a.clue: Sam puts money in and sends money out.

b.q: Priya wants to open a bakery in Hobart but needs $40,000 for ovens. Which service could a credit union offer her?
opts: A loan to buy the ovens
A deposit account to hold the ovens
A payment to the oven maker for free
A building society to sell her the ovens
b.why: Lending money to businesses is one of the services these institutions provide, so a loan fits Priya's need. A deposit account only holds money she already has, so it cannot supply the missing $40,000.
b.clue: Priya needs money she does not have yet.

a.best: Keeping his money safe and making a payment

b.best: A loan to buy the ovens

problems.detail: The distractors are absurd: a building society selling ovens, a deposit account holding ovens, or a free payment to the oven maker. A student can rule them out without knowing the idea, so the question tests almost nothing.

The distractor 'Keeping his money safe and borrowing from him' is not strictly false. A deposit is, in effect, money the institution borrows from the saver, which links to point 2. A careful student could be confused. A clearly wrong service would be safer.

check.summary: The card and the answers are correct. Question b's distractors are too absurd to test understanding. In question a, the 'borrowing from him' distractor is arguably defensible, because a deposit is money the institution borrows from the saver.

opts: Keeping his money safe and making a payment
Lending him money and making a payment
Keeping his money safe and lending him money
Lending him money to pay his phone bill

b.q: Priya wants to open a bakery in Hobart but needs $40,000 for ovens she cannot yet afford. Which service from a credit union would meet this need?
opts: A loan to pay for the ovens
A deposit account to save her takings
A transfer to pay the oven maker now
Card payments so customers can pay her
b.why: Lending gives businesses money they do not have yet, so a loan meets Priya's need. A transfer is tempting, but it only moves money she already has, and she does not have the $40,000.
b.clue: Priya needs money she does not have yet.
